drivers.name: Barco ClickShare CX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Wireless presentation Base Unit control via local REST API V2 (HTTPS, port 4003). System status, standby / wake / reboot, audio + video + wallpaper + CEC, paired-button readback. Covers CX-20 / CX-30 / CX-50, C-5 / C-10 / C-10A, CB-Core / CB-Pro.

help.overview: The ClickShare Base Unit exposes a local REST API on port 4003 (HTTPS). Use this driver to mirror runtime status (is anyone sharing?), force the Base Unit into / out of standby, reboot, and switch audio output / wallpaper / video mode under macro control. Typical room logic: when the room shutdown macro fires, send `standby`; when the room comes up, send `wakeup` (or rely on the Base Unit's auto-wake on first share).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Base Unit — its
   Ethernet MAC is on the bottom label. Leave port 4003 open between
   the OpenAVC server and the Base Unit.
2. In the Base Unit's web Configurator (https://<base-unit>), open
   Security → Pin Code / API and confirm the API is enabled. Default
   credentials are integrator / integrator. Change them and supply
   the new ones below.
3. (Recommended) Replace the self-signed HTTPS certificate with one
   trusted by the OpenAVC host, then flip "Verify SSL Certificate"
   on. The driver works either way; verifying is just defense in
   depth.
4. Click Save. The driver polls every 30 seconds by default — drop
   to 10 s if you need faster sharing-state updates (the Base Unit
   can handle it; ClickShare's own integrations poll more frequently).

compatible_models.notes: Same V2 REST API across the entire CX / C / CB family. Feature differences (number of paired buttons, dual video outputs on CX-50 Gen2, UVC pass-through on CX-30 Gen2 / CX-50 Gen2) are reported by the Base Unit at runtime in the `supportedOutputs`, `supportedModes`, `supportedPowerModes`, etc. arrays — the driver doesn't need to know the model. Older CSE / CSC ClickShare units use a different (legacy) API and are NOT covered.

drivers.name: Mersive Solstice Pod
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Mersive Solstice Pods (and Solstice Windows Software) over the OpenControl REST API. Boot users, clear posts, suspend and wake the display, reset the on-screen key, push bulletin or emergency banners, and monitor connected users and post counts.

help.overview:
Mersive Solstice is a wireless presentation system. Users share screens, video, and media from laptops, phones, and tablets to a Solstice Pod that drives the room display.

OpenAVC controls the Pod's runtime: clear posts, boot all users at end-of-meeting, sleep / wake the display, reset the on-screen connection key, and push bulletin or emergency banners. Live state includes connected users, active posts, bandwidth, and the current screen key.

Install-time configuration (network setup, calendar integration, splash-screen images) stays in the Solstice Dashboard. RS-232 pass-thru is exposed for chained-display control via a USB-to-serial adapter on the Pod.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the Pod has Solstice Enterprise Edition. The OpenControl API is gated to Enterprise hosts.
2. In the Solstice Dashboard, set an admin password (strongly recommended — without one, any device on the network can drive this Pod).
3. Enter the Pod's IP address and admin password here. Default port is 80 (HTTP). Tick Use HTTPS for port 443; Solstice ships with a self-signed certificate which the driver does not verify.
4. Mersive recommends polling no more than once every 10 seconds. The default interval is 30 s; the minimum is 10 s.

compatible_models.notes: Requires Solstice Enterprise Edition license — Standard Edition Pods do not expose the OpenControl API. Some commands are Pod-only (reboot, hardware variant, HDMI input force-off); Windows Software hosts ignore them. Power-management / suspend / wake are Pod-only.

drivers.name: Roku (ECP)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using the External Control Protocol (ECP). Full remote surface, text entry, app launch/install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models.

help.overview: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using Roku's External Control Protocol (ECP). Provides the full remote-control surface (navigation, transport, search, and on-screen text entry), app launch and install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models. Reports power state, the currently active app, and media playback status. No Roku account, PIN, or cloud connection is required, and it works with third-party Roku TVs too.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Roku to the same network and note its IP address (Settings > Network > About, or the Roku mobile app).
2. On the Roku, set Settings > System > Control by mobile apps > Network access to 'Default' or 'Permissive' (NOT 'Disabled'). Roku OS 14.1 and later block remote key presses when this is off; the driver then reports Mobile Control Enabled = false and key presses return HTTP 403.
3. Enter the IP address. The port is 8060 (do not change).
4. No PIN, password, or account is needed.
5. To launch an app, use Launch App with its channel ID. Find an installed app's ID by opening it and reading the Active App ID state, or browse http://<roku-ip>:8060/query/apps in a browser. Common IDs: Netflix 12, Amazon Prime Video 13.

compatible_models.notes: Any Roku device with 'Control by mobile apps' enabled, including third-party Roku TVs (TCL, Hisense, onn, etc.). Power, volume, and input/tuner keys apply to models that report supports-tv-power-control.
